name: Peking Opera Lianpu
summary: The symbolic facial makeup system of Peking opera where colors and patterns represent character traits and social status.
description: Lianpu features bold, symmetrical designs with symbolic colors red for loyalty, black for integrity, and white for treachery, applied in stylized patterns that enhance facial expressions. This visual language developed over centuries to help audiences quickly identify character roles in the absence of close-up viewing in traditional opera houses.
culturalContext: Peking opera's lianpu face-paint — color-coded character ideology — reads at the back row: red for loyalty (Guan Yu), black for uprightness (Bao Zheng, Zhang Fei), white for treachery (Cao Cao), blue for bravery, gold for gods and demons; the patterns (whole-face, three-tile, cross-door,歪脸) are fixed canon transmitted by master painters. Face-paint books (Weng Ouhong studies) document the grammar; the lianpu motif is Chinese opera's most exported graphic identity.
